description: IR-2/CR-2 child immigrant visa interview preparation rules using the current IR-2 questionnaire keys and question-bank categories.

designPrinciples.philosophy: Select child-visa questions by qualifying legal relationship (biological, step, adopted), age stage, household and caretaking reality, education status, travel/refusal risk, and relocation plan clarity.
designPrinciples.baseQuestions: Core applicant-petitioner relationship, family/household, education/personal background, travel/immigration history, and relocation/future-plans categories are eligible for every completed IR-2 profile.
designPrinciples.selectiveAdditions: Relationship-subtype categories (Biological Child, Stepchild, Adopted Child) are only added when the intake reports that relationship type; question-level conditions then narrow individual questions.
designPrinciples.conditionalsWork: Rules use only current questionnaire keys and values from ir-2-child/questionnaire.json, and includeCategories match ir-2-child/question-bank.json category names exactly.

selectionStrategy.approach: Layered category filtering with risk-based priority boosts.

questionSelectionRules.name: Critical IR-2 foundation - petitioner, relationship, household, education, travel, and relocation
questionSelectionRules.description: Every IR-2 interview needs the child to know who petitioned, the qualifying parent-child relationship, who they live with now, their schooling, any travel or immigration history, and the plan for living in the United States.

actions.reason: Core IR-2 readiness requires petitioner identity, qualifying relationship proof, current household facts, personal background, admissibility screening, and a coherent settlement plan.

questionSelectionRules.name: Biological child cases - establish legal parent-child relationship
questionSelectionRules.description: Biological child IR-2 cases require preparation around parents' identity and marital history, who raised the child, co-residence with the petitioning parent, and contact continuity.

actions.reason: Biological eligibility turns on proof of the parent-child relationship, marriage/divorce history, and a real ongoing relationship with the petitioning parent.

questionSelectionRules.name: Stepchild cases - verify marriage before age 18 and step-relationship history
questionSelectionRules.description: Stepchild eligibility depends on the marriage creating the step-relationship before the child turned 18, plus the lived relationship with the stepparent.

actions.reason: Stepchild eligibility is technical: marriage timing relative to the child's 18th birthday and the authenticity of the step-family relationship must be consistent and document-backed.

questionSelectionRules.name: Adopted child cases - verify adoption timing, custody, and residence with the adoptive parent
questionSelectionRules.description: Adopted child IR-2 cases require careful preparation around adoption finalization age, two-year custody and residence, and the adoptive parent's caregiving role.

actions.reason: Adoption-based eligibility needs proof of a valid adoption plus custody and joint-residence history; it should never be treated like a simple biological-child case.

questionSelectionRules.name: Unclear relationship type - cover every qualifying-route question
questionSelectionRules.description: When the relationship type is 'Other / Not Sure', the case may still be a biological, step, or adoption route, so all subtype categories are made eligible; question-level conditions and the officer's record determine what is actually asked.

actions.reason: An unclear qualifying relationship is itself a preparation risk; the child should be ready for relationship-proof questions of every kind until the route is confirmed.

questionSelectionRules.name: Living with other parent or guardian - explain current caretaking arrangement
questionSelectionRules.description: If the child does not currently live with the petitioning parent, the interview will explore who provides daily care and why the separation exists.

actions.reason: Living apart from the petitioner makes the current caretaking arrangement and the post-arrival support plan central interview topics.

questionSelectionRules.name: Frequent contact - validate current parent-child bond
questionSelectionRules.description: Daily or weekly communication supports an active family relationship and helps the child answer recent-contact questions confidently.

actions.reason: Frequent communication is positive evidence of an ongoing relationship and anchors the last-contact answer.

questionSelectionRules.name: Limited or no contact - relationship continuity needs closer explanation
questionSelectionRules.description: Occasional, rare, or no contact shifts interview focus onto who raised the child, how the relationship was maintained, and why reunification is happening now.

actions.reason: Weak contact can raise credibility questions about the relationship; the child should be prepared to explain the history truthfully and comfortably.

questionSelectionRules.name: No prior U.S. travel - basic admissibility and expectation review
questionSelectionRules.description: Children who never travelled to the U.S. still need preparation for standard travel, status, and future-plan questions.

actions.reason: No U.S. history is favorable, but the child should still answer travel and intent questions clearly and consistently.

questionSelectionRules.name: Prior U.S. visit or residence - prepare dates, status, and consistency
questionSelectionRules.description: Any past visit, residence, or current presence in the U.S. creates records the officer can check; the child should recall trips, duration, and status accurately.

anyOf.value: Yes, previously lived in the U.S.

actions.reason: Prior U.S. records are visible to the officer; travel dates, purposes, and any status history must be described consistently.

questionSelectionRules.name: Visa refusal reported - explain outcome, reason, and what changed
questionSelectionRules.description: A reported refusal (Yes or Not Sure) requires the child to be ready to describe which visa, when, and the reason given, without contradicting consular records.

actions.reason: Refusals stay in the record; preparation must cover the refusal type, date, stated reason, and how the current case differs.

questionSelectionRules.name: Refusal type identified - drill the specific refusal scenario
questionSelectionRules.description: When the refused visa category is known, follow-up questioning about that refusal becomes more specific and should be rehearsed.

actions.reason: Knowing the exact refused visa type lets the child prepare a precise, age-appropriate explanation of that decision.

questionSelectionRules.name: Possible immigration violation - maximum admissibility scrutiny
questionSelectionRules.description: A reported or uncertain overstay/status violation creates serious admissibility exposure; every answer about compliance history must be truthful and consistent.

actions.reason: Violation history affects admissibility and may involve waivers; the child must disclose plainly and understand the family's explanation.

questionSelectionRules.name: Removal or deportation history - prepare for detailed questioning
questionSelectionRules.description: Any prior removal, deportation, or entry denial is central to the case and will be explored in depth by the officer.

actions.reason: Removal history carries bars and waiver complexity; preparation should cover what happened, when, and the current legal status honestly.

questionSelectionRules.name: Minor applicants - prioritize caregiver, custody, and household questions
questionSelectionRules.description: For applicants under 18, interviews lean heavily on who cares for them, custody arrangements, and the daily-life plan, with age-appropriate wording.

actions.reason: Younger children face softer but more personal questioning about home life, caretakers, and school; rehearsing these answers reduces interview stress.

questionSelectionRules.name: Married applicant - immediate eligibility risk under IR-2
questionSelectionRules.description: IR-2 requires the child to be unmarried; a reported marriage is a critical inconsistency with the petition itself.

actions.reason: Marriage normally ends IR-2 eligibility; the interview will test this directly, so the applicant must be prepared for pointed questions and should discuss the situation with the petitioner's attorney.

questionSelectionRules.name: Stepeship marriage timing unclear or late - verify the before-18 requirement
questionSelectionRules.description: If the marriage to the stepparent happened after the child turned 18 or the timing is unsure, stepchild eligibility is at risk and needs careful preparation.

actions.reason: The step-relationship must be created before the child's 18th birthday; timing doubts make marriage-date questions central and should prompt a legal review of the case.

questionSelectionRules.name: Defined adoption route - verify the specific adoption requirements
questionSelectionRules.description: When a specific adoption route is reported, preparation should cover that route's technical requirements: age at adoption, two-year custody and residence, or Hague/orphan process steps.

anyOf.value: Adopted Under the Sibling Exception Before Age 18

actions.reason: Each adoption route has distinct legal tests (full and final adoption, custody plus residence, or Convention process) that shape the officer's questions.

questionSelectionRules.name: Currently studying - school continuity questions
questionSelectionRules.description: Children enrolled in school should be ready to discuss their grade, school, and plans to continue education in the United States.

actions.reason: School details are a natural line of questioning for student applicants and support the resettlement plan.

questionSelectionRules.name: Applicant has siblings - family composition questions
questionSelectionRules.description: Siblings may be part of related petitions or family records, so their names and locations should be ready to state.

actions.reason: Sibling details test family-composition consistency with the petition and civil records.

migrationNotes.v1_to_v1.0.0: Fully rebuilt to match the current ir-2-child questionnaire keys (applicant_age_range, currently_studying, has_siblings, petitioner_relationship, child_relationship_type, biological_parent_petitioner, biological_parents_married_at_birth, stepparent_marriage_before_18, adoption_case_type, current_living_arrangement, communication_frequency, us_travel_history, previous_visa_refusal, refused_visa_type, immigration_violation, deportation_removal_history) and the v2 question-bank categories. Removed obsolete fields such as current_country, current_age (numeric), lived_with_parent, relationship_type, sponsor_relationship, criminal_history, communication_method, has_photos_with_parent, financial_support_from_parent, plans_to_study, and the old category names (Basic Identity, Special Cases, Intent, Security, etc.).
